subject: Novarine launch: temporary ingress entitlement & traffic scenarios
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@novarine.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Novarine launch: temporary ingress entitlement & traffic scenarios

Hi team / Sophie,

Thanks again for the sync earlier. Novarine is set to run a public beta starting 2025-05-01 with a high-probability surge window in the first 72 hours. Attached is the mutual action plan (Novarine_MAP_v1.xlsx) and the projected ingress profile (ingress_projection_Q42025.csv). Key asks from Novarine: a temporary ingress uplift to 2x their committed baseline for a 72-hour warmup, a short-term rate window increase on the chat/text-generation route, and visibility into per-route latency and token-level cost during that period.

Ask of the product/ops group: can we provision a temporary entitlement (non-billable credit or soft quota) scoped to Novarine's account and route: /v1/generate-chat? If so, what exact knobs do we need to flip (prewarm KV cache, reserve N concurrent slots, allow continuous batching)? Sophie — can you confirm peak TPS and average prompt length? I used conservative estimates in the CSV but will adjust if you share numbers.

Proposed timeline:
- 2025-04-20: product/engineering sign-off on cadence and fallback policy
- 2025-04-27: capacity prewarm and staging smoke tests
- 2025-05-01 00:00 UTC: launch traffic window (72 hours)

If product needs a service-level carveout or a temporary routing policy (route to smaller quantized model when utilization > 85%), let's capture that now so sales/legal/engineering can approve.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@novarine.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Apr 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Novarine launch: temporary ingress entitlement & traffic scenarios

Vivek / Sophie — looping in ops & product to scope this. A few clarifying questions from Sales Ops before we lock an entitlement: 

1) Baseline + uplift: Vivek, can you confirm the committed baseline (tokens/min or qps) in HubSpot? I see a trial commitment listed but need the numeric baseline to calculate buffer.
2) Route specificity: Is the traffic going to a single route (/v1/generate-chat) or split across embeddings/qa/rerank? The projection currently assumes 85% chat, 10% embeddings, 5% rerank.
3) Failover behavior: Are we comfortable with an automatic fallback to the quantized-smaller model if latency degrades, or do we want hard throttles and 429s for fair-share?

Operational asks for Product/Infra: 
- Temporary quota window: +2x baseline for 72h with a start timestamp (to be set by Ops).
- Telemetry slice: token-level cost and per-route latency with 1-min granularity for the 72h window.
- Prewarm: prepopulate KV cache for the top 200 prompt prefixes, and reserve 4 dedicated inference slots for expected warm-up bursts.

Grace / David — is the above feasible from a runtime perspective? If we need a canary policy (ingress ramp 0->50% first 2 hours -> 100%), call that out and we'll coordinate with Novarine.

Karthik
Sales Ops Lead
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Novarine launch: temporary ingress entitlement & traffic scenarios

Thanks — quick technical read and product asks below. High-level: we can support a time-boxed entitlement, but we need explicit fallback logic and a prewarm plan or cost will spike.

Product/infra notes and asks:
- Fallback: we strongly prefer an automated model-variant fallback (route -> chat-medium-quant) at 80% GPU utilization per-pool rather than blanket throttling. That keeps availability for heavy customers and maintains degraded but usable responses.
- Prewarm: ops should trigger a KV cache prewarm job 24h before the start window; list of top prefixes must be finalized by Sophie by 2025-04-24.
- Batching: enable continuous batching for the route with a 20ms max latency buffer; this will save tokens and reduce cost at the expense of minimal added latency.
- Reserved slots: we'll reserve 3 slots in the dedicated pool and allow burst to shared capacity if utilization remains <65%.
- Telemetry: we can expose per-route latency/percentile dashboards. For token-cost visibility, we'll surface per-minute token counts and estimated cost; engineering needs a signed-off SSO view for Novarine if they want direct access.

Operational constraints:
- If the projected 95th percentile load exceeds the reserved+burst capacity, we need to run the canary-ramp 0->50% over 2h. If Novarine declines the canary we will instead enforce a hard quota at 150% of baseline and return 429s once exceeded.

Next steps (action owners):
- Sophie (Novarine): confirm top prefixes and actual peak TPS by 2025-04-22.
- Karthik (Sales Ops): confirm baseline numbers in HubSpot and whether Novarine needs SSO access to dashboards by 2025-04-21.
- David (Infra): schedule prewarm job and reserve slots; confirm whether 3 slots are sufficient by 2025-04-18.
- Vivek (AE): finalize MAP and push mutual sign-off.

Grace O'Connor
Product Manager, Serving Runtime
grace_oconnor@redwood.com

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@novarine.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Apr 2025 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Novarine launch: temporary ingress entitlement & traffic scenarios

Quick status update from infra — we can execute the temporal uplift but a couple of infra-level clarifications: 

1) Dedicated pool vs shared burst: reserving 3 slots in the dedicated pool is fine for baseline; for the proposed 2x uplift we'll need to allow burst to shared nodes for ~18 hours of the 72h window unless Novarine agrees to a larger reserved commit (which they likely won't for a beta).
2) Model fallback implementation: we can pin a routing policy that checks GPU pool utilization and swaps to chat-medium-quant at 80% utilization. That requires a short maintenance window (30m) to deploy the policy and add the variant to Novarine's account.
3) Telemetry hooks: we'll flip on per-route high-frequency metrics — expect a 10% increase in metric ingestion cost during the window; ops confirms this in the MAP so Finance is aware.

I'll schedule the prewarm job for 2025-04-30 03:00 UTC and will post the runbook in JIRA-OPS-1298. If Novarine wants guaranteed headroom without shared bursting, we need a short commercial amendment.

David Kim
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
